A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same reward-model inference study despite the changed title and OCTS-to-CRISP renaming. Their main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original reward-model diagnostic experiments, OCTS benchmark evaluations, and component ablations, including Tables 1, 7, and 8.

after.justification: V2 retains original experiments and adds R1 comparisons, additional task and reward-model evaluations, computational-cost measurements, sensitivity studies, and repeated-run results.

M1.justification: The substantive procedure is retained: complete-path sampling, answer-based clustering, summed cluster rewards, early stopping for few distinct answers, and regeneration from selected step prefixes. V1's three OCTS stages become five CRISP modules. The expanded equations, normalization disclosure, and pseudocode do not establish a substantive algorithm revision.

E1.justification: V2 adds LogiQA logical reading-comprehension tasks and SIQA social reasoning in Sections 4.3–4.4, substantially extending the evaluated task requirements. The earlier mathematical benchmarks and appendix probes are retained. Commonsense and logical reasoning were not entirely absent from v1: its appendix already evaluated CSQA, WinoGrande, ProofWriter, and ProntoQA.

E2.justification: V2 Table 2 introduces direct comparisons against DeepSeek-R1-Distill and corresponding Chat models on two Qwen2.5-Math backbones, expanding beyond v1's search and voting comparisons. The Qwen2.5-3B OlympiadBench comparison also gains CoT and PRM-based BoN Weighted entries relative to v1 Figure 22.

E3.justification: V2 adds matched-backbone Chat/R1/CRISP comparisons with output-length measurement, controlled runtime/token-cost evaluations, additional reward-model configurations, and dataset-defined difficulty partitions. Appendix L reports 500 GSM8K/MATH questions where v1 Appendix G specified 200 for Llama3.1-8B; this changes the reported setting without establishing reruns. The preliminary MATH comparison also drops Llama2-13B and Mistral-7B.

E4.justification: New analyses examine CRISP's sample count, top-k selection, stopping threshold, and maximum steps (Tables 11–14), ablations across reward models (Table 18), dataset-defined difficulty (Table 7), and the time–accuracy tradeoff (Figure 30). V1's original ablation values are retained in v2 Figure 28; many diagnostic plots are relocated rather than newly added.

E5.justification: V2 Appendix O and Tables 15–17 newly report five MATH runs for Qwen2.5-3B with Skyworko1, individual-run accuracies, variances, 95% confidence intervals, and t-tests. V1 contains graphical uncertainty bands and error bars but no corresponding repeated-run significance assessment of the main comparison. Its run count is not established.

E6.justification: Most GSM8K/MATH entries from v1 Tables 1 and 7 are retained with rounding. Genuine revisions include Qwen2.5-3B OlympiadBench OCTS/CRISP ORM/PRM accuracies changing from 0.34/0.35 to 0.36/0.39, and MCTS from 0.305/0.34 to 0.34/0.31 (v1 Figure 22; v2 Table 1). V2 also adds substantial R1, cost, sensitivity, and repeated-run results.

T1.justification: V2 Appendix K adds a short derivation relating cluster-score ratios to answer frequencies and average rewards, beyond v1's intuitive rationale. This is a limited conditional mathematical argument, not a general guarantee. Its concluding inequality is reversed relative to Equation 8, weakening the added reasoning.

C1.justification: The three diagnostic claims remain, but v2 prominently positions inference-time optimization against training-centric reasoning and adds claims about non-mathematical gains over R1 and substantial token savings. The advertised maximum accuracy advantage rises from 3.2% to 5%; however, the five-point Llama3.1-8B MATH advantage already appeared in v1 Table 7.

C2.justification: V2 interprets the new comparisons as evidence of stronger task generalization and more efficient reasoning, while acknowledging inferior mathematical accuracy to R1. It adds task-dependent hyperparameter guidance and a qualification that clustering benefits from frequent correct answers. The limitations section removes v1's stated exclusion of commonsense/logical analysis while retaining the unexamined training-phase limitation.

D1.justification: V2 supplies explicit pseudocode, six complete prompt templates (Tables 19–24), NVIDIA A100 hardware information, reward-normalization details, an explicit repository link, and a reproducibility statement. V1 already documented most default search hyperparameters and referred to prompts in accompanying software; the added PDF documentation is substantially more self-contained. Repository availability itself is not verified.

R1.justification: The introduction substantially reframes the work around inference-time optimization versus RL/SFT and R1-style reasoning, incorporating overthinking and generalization concerns. New citations include s1, LIMO, Logic-RL, and related efficiency/generalization studies. DeepSeek-R1 was already cited in v1; the major difference is its expanded role in the paper's positioning.

P1.justification: V2 extensively rewrites the abstract and introduction, retitles the paper, renames OCTS, consolidates v1's three diagnostic sections into Section 3, and rewrites the method as five modules. Several analyses move into reorganized appendices, while limitations, reproducibility, and language-assistance disclosures receive separate placement.

P2.justification: The paper changes from two-column to single-column formatting, redraws the method diagram as a worked five-module example, restructures Figure 1, and combines formerly separate main and appendix results into Table 1. Numerous plots are relocated or split, the original ablation table becomes Figure 28, and new comparison tables, statistical tables, and prompt displays are added.

improvement.justification: The repeated-run comparisons, sensitivity tests, broader evaluations, and printed prompts strengthen empirical support and reproducibility. The net gain is limited by defects in the new material: Appendix K reverses its key inequality, Algorithm 1 loops on sample count n rather than maximum steps m, and Table 4 and Figure 29b report unexplained, differently ranked token costs. These problems weaken the new theoretical and efficiency claims without overturning the retained empirical contribution.
